paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God wants His house to be a house of prayer, and Jesus cares about what is really going on inside it. He walks into the temple courts and says, "My house will be called a house of prayer," but they are making it "a den of robbers." (Matthew 21:13) Then look who He lets come close: the blind and the lame, and He heals them (Matthew 21:14). The place built for meeting God was supposed to be open to people who need Him.

Now look at the two reactions. The chief priests and scribes were indignant, but the children were shouting, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" (Matthew 21:15). Jesus says, "From the mouths of children and infants You have ordained praise" (Matthew 21:16). I think the lesson is about the heart. Leaves and busy activity look good from the road, but Jesus came looking for fruit, and the fig tree had "nothing on it except leaves" (Matthew 21:19). Being around holy things is not the same as honoring them, and I know what a stamper looks like when he's all show, friend.

So what do we do with that? Jesus tells His disciples, "if you have faith and do not doubt," the impossible can happen, even a mountain thrown into the sea (Matthew 21:21). Then He says, "If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer." (Matthew 21:22) That brings the whole passage together: God's house is for prayer, and He invites you to come to Him in faith. So bring your real requests to Him, baker, and don't settle for just looking busy.
